item.title: Rapid and Accurate Quantification of Microplastics in Surface Water using Improved YOLO Model
item.description:
📚 Preprints
👤 Hanbin Yang, Haoyu Wang, Fang Tao, Hailu Fu, Jie Yu, Jie Ouyang 等10位作者
Microplastics (MPs), widespread emerging pollutants across the globe, impose serious threats to ecosystems and human health. To fully unravel their complex environmental behaviors and advance pollution governance, high-efficiency, high-precision monitoring techniques are urgently required. Given the major analytical obstacles arising from faint optical signals and highly variable morphologies of MPs in environmental matrices, this work introduces YOLO-MPs, a physics-guided deep learning framework designed to rapidly and precisely quantify five common MPs types (fibers, fragments, films, pellets and linear pieces) collected from surface water. item.title: 通过倾斜 MnTe 自旋源中的自旋传播与极化实现全电磁化翻转
item.description:
📚 Nature Communications
👤 Yu Dai, Yandong Guo, Yuanyuan Jiang, Yongsen Zhang, Tianping Ma, Boyu Li 等11位作者

item.title: Multi-scale characterization of pore structure in deep coal and rock reservoirs and evaluation of movable fluids
item.description:

The pore structure of deep coal and rock reservoirs is complex. Traditional single methods are difficult to comprehensively characterize them, and fluid mobility cannot be evaluated. item.title: Integrated Electrical Resistivity and Transient Electromagnetic Investigation for Groundwater Aquifer Characterization in the Western Desert Fringes: A Case Study of Gabal El-Nashfa Area, El-Minya Governorate, Egypt
item.description:

Groundwater represents the main water resource in the Egyptian Western Desert (EWD) which is considered a finite and strategic resource. These limited resources are the critical hydrological driver for large-scale sustainable development initiatives, including strategic agriculture and renewable energy projects, which are vital components of Egypt's national water and food security strategy. item.title: Geometry and Structural Controls on the Magmatic Emplacement and Geo-spatial Distribution of the San Feliciano Plutonic System, Northern Zacatecas, Mexico: Insights from Integrated Aeromagnetic Modelling and Geological Constraints
item.description:
📚 Preprints
👤 Erik Emmanuel M. Torres, Héctor López-Loera, Sanjeet K. Verma, Eduardo G. Partida, Mahendra Shukla
The San Feliciano Plutonic System is an intermediate composition and syn-tectonic Late Cretaceous magmatic system located in northern Zacatecas, Mexico, emplaced within a Mesozoic marine sedimentary sequence. The origin of the SFPS is directly related to the genesis of Concepción del Oro Intrusive Belt (COIB), a magmatic province which comprises several plutonic systems associated to the development of the Cretaceous–Eocene Mexican Magmatic Arc (CEMMA) formed during the subduction of the Farallon Plate beneath the North American Plate. During this period, the deformation of the continental crust, specifically in the study area, was developed as a consequence of the tectonic compression by the Mexican Orogen. item.title: Embedded platinum channels bring nanoscale spin-based thermoelectric conversion to bulk materials
item.description:
📚 Physics News
A joint research team from NIMS and the University of Tokyo has developed a new composite in which three-dimensional nano-interfaces are distributed throughout the material by coating the surfaces of magnetic-insulator powders with a metal and sintering them. Using this structure, the team succeeded in observing thermoelectric conversion driven by spins in an insulator, a phenomenon previously observed only at nanoscale thin-film interfaces, in a macroscale material.

item.title: Levitated magnet opens new frontier in search for ultraheavy dark matter
item.description:
📚 Physics News
Rice University researchers have used a magnetically levitated particle to search for ultraheavy dark matter, extending the hunt for some of the heaviest possible forms of the invisible matter thought to hold galaxies together. Led by Christopher Tunnell, associate professor of physics and astronomy, the researchers used a tiny floating magnet as a highly sensitive detector designed to register the faint push an ultraheavy dark matter particle could produce as it passed through.

item.title: Magic-angle graphene provides evidence for unconventional superconductivity
item.description:
📚 Physics News
Researchers have completely suppressed superconductivity in magic-angle graphene by screening interactions between electrons, helping resolve a long-running debate about the origin of the phenomenon.

item.title: Unconditional and exponentially large violation of classicality
item.description:
📚 Nature Communications

Nature Communications, Published online: 05 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-77413-3 The authors introduce a practical game that distinguishes quantum from classical behaviour without relying on unproven assumptions. Quantum computers achieve exponentially larger scores than any classical strategy, a result confirmed in experiments.
